title: The Lake Above the Pass

setup.context: Let me tell you about the lake above the pass. The shepherds call it Darpan, the mirror. I went there the year after the fall.

paragraphs.text: The walk takes four days from the last road, through pine forest and then across grey scree to a valley with no trees at all. At the top there is a lake so still that the sky sits on it like a second sky.
The shepherds who guide us don't talk much. On the second night one of them told me that the lake only shows you what you bring. I thought it was a nice line, the sort of thing you say to tourists.

I sat at the shore for most of an afternoon. The wind dropped, the water went glass-smooth, and I saw my own face clearly for the first time in a year. It looked tired, and older than I had imagined. It also looked calm.
I can't tell you the lake did anything to me. I can tell you I walked down the next morning more slowly than I walked up, and that I have been slower since.

reflection.insight: A place can slow you down, but it cannot do the slowing for you. The stillness you find there is stillness you were already able to reach.
reflection.question: Is there a place where you can actually see your own face clearly?

follow_up_options: Did the shepherds believe the lake was special?
Would you take someone else there?

responses_to_follow_ups.danger: It is demanding, especially the scree. Good boots, a guide, and enough respect for the altitude. You don't need to be fit to start, but you need to be honest about your limits.
responses_to_follow_ups.believe: They believe a great many things and do not argue about them. I learned more from their silence than from anything they said.
responses_to_follow_ups.take: Only someone who wants to walk slowly. Everyone else will be disappointed, and will be right to be.

practical_note: If you ever walk up there, walk slowly and go with a guide you trust.
